title: [WT-04] Wrappers: provision the task worktree at worker pre-flight
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §1.1-§1.6, the §6.5 worker stop and the §7.2 guards.

Objective: a worker seat whose claim says worktree mode gets its own locked, sparse git worktree W on moe/task/<taskId>, or stops loudly. It never falls back to the shared checkout. Shared mode is unchanged (epic rail 4).

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins, worker seats only:
- Read `workspace` from the claim response (fresh claim) or get_context (resume), per WT-01/WT-02 (task-e27456ad67b64bc292080ea3a8b92f26). An absent field (older daemon) means shared mode.
- In worktree mode, run the guards before any W work. Each failure calls report_blocked with its code and stops the seat:
  - git >= 2.38: MOE_WORKTREE_UNSUPPORTED_GIT
  - project is the git top level: MOE_WORKTREE_PROJECT_NOT_TOP
  - control checkout HEAD is refs/heads/moe/control: MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING
  - task bytes on a shared branch that the target lacks: MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH
  - Windows path budget: MOE_WORKTREE_PATH_TOO_LONG
- Create W with `git worktree add --lock --reason "moe <taskId>" --no-checkout -b moe/task/<taskId> W refs/heads/<target>` (cut from the LOCAL target; WT-09 adds the fetch), then `sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.moe/'`, then `read-tree -mu HEAD`.
- Reuse W when `git worktree list --porcelain` shows it (D:\ vs /mnt/d normalized), running `worktree repair` on a cross-OS reuse. Re-add W on an existing branch without -b. Warn MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT if W/.moe exists.
- Any git failure: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED. Remove only a half-made W with no commits beyond the target, report_blocked, no CLI launch.
- In shared mode, an existing moe/task/<taskId> that is not fully landed means MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH and report_blocked. Add the 'fully landed' helper sh task_branch_landed / ps1 Test-MoeTaskBranchLanded (merge-tree of target and branch equals the target's tree, §1.7); WT-14 reuses it.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1.

NOT in scope:
- CLI cwd, env and configs (WT-05)
- links and Serena (WT-06)
- any landing (WT-07 onward)
- the control follow and auto-switch (WT-13)
- removal and sweep (WT-14)
- docs (WT-18)

Chained after task-5998f871e03d4ed5ab21f214073d85b2, which edits the same wrappers.

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses): a worktree-mode worker claim creates a locked worktree at .worktrees/<taskId> on moe/task/<taskId>, W/.moe does not exist, and the control checkout's HEAD, index and files are unchanged.
postflight case: a second session of the same task reuses W (no new worktree add, its dirt intact); with the branch present but W missing, W is re-added on that branch without -b.
postflight cases: each guard (git < 2.38 via a stub, project not top level, control not on moe/control, mode mismatch) prints its code, calls report_blocked and launches no CLI.
postflight case: shared mode with an unlanded moe/task/<taskId> prints MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH; shared mode without one behaves exactly as before (existing cases unchanged).

Both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes: diff of `grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*'` over moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 (sort -u) is empty.
node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh exits 0; postflight.ps1 passes via node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell.

implementationPlan.description:
Rename the sh python bridge env names out of the MOE_LAND_ family. This is the DoD 5 enabler.

At HEAD, DoD 5's `grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*'` already differs between the twins. resolve_attribution in moe-agent.sh passes values from bash to its inline python through nine sh-only env names, 19 occurrences in all:
- MOE_LAND_UNDECLARED, MOE_LAND_CONTESTED, MOE_LAND_EXCLUDE
- MOE_LAND_BOARD_STATE, MOE_LAND_POLICY_OVERRIDE, MOE_LAND_BASE
- MOE_LAND_INDEX, MOE_LAND_EVIDENCE, MOE_LAND_PREFLIGHT_DIRTY

They are internal plumbing, not codes: parity-check already exempts names of this kind, and the ps1 twin has no python bridge.

Rename each MOE_LAND_<X> to MOE_PY_<X> at all 19 occurrences. MOE_PY_ is unused today and outside every compared family, now and after WT-19 adds its families. The occurrences are the env prefix lines of resolve_attribution and every env.get(...) in its python. Nothing else in the file changes.

Apply the same mapping in the two tests that run the extracted python with these env names. A missed occurrence there silently falls back to a default:
- scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs: 5 occurrences, in the env objects near lines 51-52 and 206.
- scripts/tests/usage-attribution.test.mjs: 6 occurrences, the PowerShell snippet's $env:MOE_LAND_UNDECLARED near line 34 and the env object near lines 82-83.

Leave scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1's comment that mentions MOE_LAND_* names alone. WT-19 owns parity-check.

Saving moe-agent.sh: running bash seats keep reading it by byte offset (Serena gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse).
- Write the whole new file to a scratch path on the same filesystem, /mnt/d/moe-scratch/c20464ff/moe-agent.sh.
- Run `bash -n` on it.
- Replace the live file with one `mv -f`. Never write it partially in place.
- The same rule holds for every later save of moe-agent.sh in this task.

Test:
- `grep -c 'MOE_LAND_'` prints 0 for each of the three files.
- `node --test scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs scripts/tests/usage-attribution.test.mjs` passes. Both run in CI's script-test jobs.

This step's error handling: if either test fails, the cause is a missed or misspelled occurrence. Fix the mapping, never the test's assertions.

Hook the held-out suite into both harnesses, next to the owner-guard suite it is modelled on. The suite is scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs from WT-04T (task-dd5daa4b789645d29b192176390884be). This row stays unclaimable until WT-04T lands.

Do NOT edit the suite or scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js. They are held-out tests, and QA rejects any change to them. If a held-out case is wrong, call moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ["task-dd5daa4b789645d29b192176390884be"] and the evidence. Never work around it.

scripts/tests/postflight.sh: directly after the line that runs postflight-owner-guard.cjs, add

"$NODE_FOR_TEST" "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs" sh "$WRAPPER" "$FAKE_PROXY" "$TMP_DIR" "$(command -v bash)"

The harness runs under set -e, so the suite's exit 1 fails it.

No other byte of either harness changes. DoD 4 requires the existing cases unchanged.

Test: run the suite directly against the current wrappers to record the red baseline:
```
node scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs sh scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$(mktemp -d)" "$(command -v bash)"
```
Every case except shared-landed should fail, as WT-04T recorded. Steps 3 and 4 turn it green.

sh implementation in scripts/moe-agent.sh, covering DoD 1-4 on the sh engine. The contract is the one in WT-04T's description (task-dd5daa4b789645d29b192176390884be). Its suite is the arbiter and stays unchanged.

Add three functions right after git_top().

1. task_branch_landed REF TASKID
- Returns 0 only when `git -C "$MOE_TOP" merge-tree --write-tree "$REF" "refs/heads/moe/task/$TASKID"` exits 0 AND its first output line equals `git -C "$MOE_TOP" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$REF^{tree}"`.
- Any failure returns 1, meaning not landed: git older than 2.38, an unknown ref, or a conflict.
- Header comment says three things. Ancestry can't be the test, because a worktree completion lands as a squash commit (design §1.7). WT-14 reuses this with REF=refs/heads/<target>. The twin is Test-MoeTaskBranchLanded.

2. worktree_stop CODE DETAIL
- Print `echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1: $2"`.
- Build {taskId: $PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID, workerId: $WORKER_ID, reason: "$1: $2"} with $PYTHON_CMD json.dumps over argv. Never splice JSON as a string.
- Send it with `moe_rpc report_blocked`. If building or sending fails, print one `${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} moe.report_blocked failed for $PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID; the seat stops anyway.` line.
- Then stop_heartbeat_sidecar and `exit 1`. The EXIT trap deregisters, as it does for MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED.
- Never call it inside $(...), a pipeline or a subshell, where exit would not end the seat.

3. provision_worktree
a. Parse. Run $PYTHON_CMD once, reading CLAIM_RESULT and PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT from env vars, not argv, because they can be large.
- ws = claim['workspace'] if it is a dict, else context['workspace'] if that is a dict, else none. Unparseable JSON counts as absent.
- Print three fields separated by \x1f:
  - mode: 'worktree' only when ws.mode == 'worktree', else 'shared';
  - target: the stripped string;
  - foreign shas, space-separated: the context's task.commits entries whose kind is checkpoint or completion, whose sha is 40-hex, and whose ref is not in {moe/task/<id>, refs/heads/moe/task/<id>, <target>, refs/heads/<target>}.
b. Shared mode. `git_top || return 0`. If `git -C "$MOE_TOP" rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/heads/moe/task/$tid"` finds the branch and `task_branch_landed HEAD "$tid"` fails, call worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH "shared-mode claim, but moe/task/$tid holds worktree bytes HEAD lacks; land or rescue that branch first". Otherwise return 0 and touch nothing (rail 4). The guard compares against HEAD, not the target, for two reasons: WT-01 sends target null in shared mode, and after a rollback (§7.4) HEAD is the shared branch the bytes must be in.
c. Worktree-mode guards, in this order, each ending in worktree_stop:
- `git --version` gives a major.minor below 2.38, or can't be parsed: MOE_WORKTREE_UNSUPPORTED_GIT "git <version> is older than 2.38; worktree mode needs git merge-tree --write-tree". Print the version git reported; the suite's stub prints 2.37.9.
- git_top fails, or MOE_REL is non-empty: MOE_WORKTREE_PROJECT_NOT_TOP.
- `git -C "$MOE_TOP" symbolic-ref -q HEAD` is not refs/heads/moe/control: MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING, naming the current HEAD. WT-13 adds the follow and the auto-switch; this task never does.
- The target is blank, or `git check-ref-format --branch "$target"` fails, or `git -C "$MOE_TOP" rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$target^{commit}"` fails: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- For any foreign sha, `git -C "$MOE_TOP" merge-base --is-ancestor "$sha" "refs/heads/$target"` is non-zero, which includes an unknown sha: MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH, naming the sha and its ref.
- Only when $OSTYPE matches msys*|cygwin*: ${#W} + 1 + the longest name from `git -C "$MOE_TOP" ls-tree -r -z --name-only "refs/heads/$target"` is over 240, and `git -C "$MOE_TOP" config --bool core.longpaths` is not true: MOE_WORKTREE_PATH_TOO_LONG.
d. Find or make W.
- W="$MOE_TOP/.worktrees/$tid" and branch="moe/task/$tid". Derive both here, never from ws.path: a Windows daemon spells it D:\..., and a WSL seat needs /mnt/d/....
- Look up W by piping `git -C "$MOE_TOP" worktree list --porcelain -z` to python. Python finds the record whose path equals W under the comparable() rule copied from probe_daemon_health (drive and UNC paths case-folded, /mnt/<d>/x equal to <d>:/x). It prints `found\x1f<raw path>\x1f<branch ref or empty>`, or `absent`. If the listing fails: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- found:
  - If the branch ref isn't refs/heads/$branch: CREATE_FAILED.
  - If the raw path differs from "$W", run `git -C "$MOE_TOP" worktree repair "$W"` first.
  - If `git -C "$W" ls-files` fails: CREATE_FAILED. If it prints nothing, a session died between add and read-tree: run the sparse and read-tree steps below.
  - verb=reused. Never run read-tree on a non-empty index; leave its dirt untouched.
- absent, and the branch exists (`rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/$branch`): `git -C "$MOE_TOP" worktree add --lock --reason "moe $tid" --no-checkout "$W" "$branch"`, verb=re-added.
- absent, and no branch: the same add with `--no-track -b "$branch" "$W" "refs/heads/$target"`, verb=created.
- After an add, run `git -C "$W" sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.moe/'`, then `git -C "$W" read-tree -mu HEAD`.
e. Error handling:
- Capture git's stderr with 2>&1 and put its first line in the CREATE_FAILED detail.
- A failed `worktree add` removes nothing: the directory may belong to someone else.
- If sparse or read-tree fails after this session's own add, check `git -C "$MOE_TOP" rev-list --count "refs/heads/$target..refs/heads/$branch"`. If it prints 0, run `git -C "$MOE_TOP" worktree remove --force --force "$W"` (the worktree is locked). Otherwise keep W; the next session's empty-index finish completes it.
- Then MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED. Never delete a branch.
f. If `[ -e "$W/.moe" ] || [ -L "$W/.moe" ]`: MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT "$W/.moe exists; a worktree never holds .moe files, so a human must inspect it". Delete nothing. Design §1.6 fails closed here and supersedes the description's "warn" (rail 3).
g. Success: set MOE_WT_MODE=worktree, MOE_WT_PATH="$W", MOE_WT_BRANCH="$branch" and MOE_WT_TARGET="$target". Print `[worktree] $verb $W on $branch`. The CLI then launches exactly as today; WT-05 moves its cwd.

Per-iteration reset: add `MOE_WT_MODE=shared; MOE_WT_PATH=""; MOE_WT_BRANCH=""; MOE_WT_TARGET=""` next to the `MOE_TOP=""` reset at the loop top.

Call site, directly above `# -------- Pre-flight landing: recovery, baseline, rescue-ref discovery --------`:
```
if [ "$AUTO_CLAIM" = true ] && [ "$PREFLIGHT_OK" = true ] && [ -n "$PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID" ] && [ "$ROLE" = worker ]; then provision_worktree; fi
```
It is not gated on autoCommit (the suite's fixtures use autoCommit:false). It runs before the pre-flight landing, so a refusal leaves no fresh baseline.

set -e is on, so every git and python call sits in an if, || or && test. No bare command may fail.

DoD 5: the seven codes appear in both twins. Put no other MOE_WORKTREE_, MOE_LAND_, MOE_CONTROL_ or MOE_BOARD_ token in code or comments; the grep reads comments too. Shell variables use the MOE_WT_ prefix.

Save the same way as step 1.

Test loop: run
```
MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=<case> node scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs sh scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$(mktemp -d)" "$(command -v bash)"
```
until every sh case prints ok.

ps1 twin in scripts/moe-agent.ps1, covering DoD 1-4 on the ps1 engine. It matches step 3's contract, guard order, codes and detail sentences, and the `[worktree] <verb> <W> on <branch>` line, character for character.

Functions:
- Add Test-MoeTaskBranchLanded([string]$Top, [string]$Ref, [string]$TaskId), Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat([string]$Code, [string]$Detail) and Initialize-MoeWorktree after Get-MoeGitTop and Invoke-MoeGit.

Git calls:
- Make every git call through Invoke-MoeGit, with -MergeStderr where the detail needs git's message. Never run a bare `& git` while $ErrorActionPreference is Stop, because PS 5.1 turns native stderr into errors.
- The version probe is a plain git invocation resolved through PATH, so the suite's git stub answers it.

Inputs:
- Mode: $claim.workspace when $claim.PSObject.Properties['workspace'] holds an object (a fresh claim), else $preflightContext.workspace. $null or a non-object counts as absent.
- Commits: $preflightContext.task.commits.
- Top and Rel come from Get-MoeGitTop, whose Top uses git's D:/ spelling. W = "$($git.Top)/.worktrees/$TaskId".

Comparisons:
- Path identity: Get-MoeComparableProjectPath on both sides, then [string]::Equals($a, $b, [StringComparison]::Ordinal) (Serena gotcha-powershell-path-comparison-culture).
- Use -ceq and -cmatch for refs and codes.
- Read the porcelain with `worktree list --porcelain -z` and split on "`0".

Guards:
- Apply the path budget whenever running on Windows: $PSVersionTable.PSVersion.Major -le 5, or $IsWindows.
- The .moe check is `$null -ne (Get-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $w '.moe') -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)`. It also sees a dangling link.

Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat:
- Write-Host "[ERROR] ${Code}: $Detail" -ForegroundColor Red.
- Call Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool 'report_blocked' -Args @{ taskId = $preflightTaskId; workerId = $WorkerId; reason = "${Code}: $Detail" } inside try/catch. On failure, print the same [WARN] sentence as sh.
- Then Stop-HeartbeatSidecar and `exit 1`. The hot-reload supervisor exits with a pass's exit code, and the pass's finally deregisters.

Wiring:
- Reset $script:MoeWtMode = 'shared' and $script:MoeWtPath, $script:MoeWtBranch and $script:MoeWtTarget to '' beside `$preflightTaskId = ""`.
- Directly above `# -------- Pre-flight baseline (land-on-every-exit) --------`, outside the autoCommit branch, add `if ($AutoClaim -and $preflightOk -and $preflightTaskId -and $Role -eq 'worker') { Initialize-MoeWorktree }`.

Error handling:
- Check the Rc of every Invoke-MoeGit result.
- A thrown error inside Initialize-MoeWorktree is caught and turned into MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED. It must never become a crash that launches the CLI or leaves the seat looping. A catch block never sees `exit`, so Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat still ends the seat.
- The removal rule matches step 3e exactly: only a W this session added whose branch has 0 commits beyond the target, and never a branch.

Saving:
- Keep the UTF-8 BOM.
- Parse with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under Windows PowerShell 5.1, the fleet host, before testing.
- An in-place save is fine for ps1, because PowerShell parses the whole file at start.

Test loop from WSL. Use MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY to narrow the run, and repeat until every ps1 case prints ok:
```
node.exe scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs ps1 scripts/moe-agent.ps1 scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$(wslpath -w "$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/wt04-ps.XXXXXX)")" powershell
```
The path-long case runs here because the host is win32.

Verification. Run this once, fresh, from the repo root in WSL. Its output tail is the complete_task evidence. It covers DoD 5 and 6, and DoD 1-4 through the suite inside both harnesses.

```
S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/v-c20464ff.XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD scripts | tar -x -C "$S" && for f in scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/moe-agent.ps1 scripts/tests/postflight.sh scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs scripts/tests/usage-attribution.test.mjs; do cp "$f" "$S/$f" && cmp "$f" "$S/$f" || exit 1; done && printf 'Verification snapshot: %s\n' "$S" && cd "$S" && diff <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*' scripts/moe-agent.sh | sort -u) <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*' scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | sort -u) && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && node --test scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs scripts/tests/usage-attribution.test.mjs && env $(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && WSLENV=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 node.exe scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell
```

What it covers:
- A HEAD snapshot of scripts/ on /mnt/d, with this task's six files copied over and cmp-checked, so peers' unlanded bytes can't leak in. It also holds WT-04T's suite and fake proxy, as landed.
- DoD 5's token diff, which must be empty.
- parity-check.
- The two node tests that use the renamed env names.
- postflight.sh through postflight-safe.mjs, with MOE_* and CLAUDE* scrubbed from the env. The seat's own MOE_WORKER_ID and MOE_SESSION_ID must not reach the wrappers under test.
- postflight.ps1 through Windows node, so postflight-safe runs it on Windows PowerShell 5.1.

On a native Windows seat, run the same chain from Git Bash with `node` in place of `node.exe`.

Each of the two harness runs takes tens of minutes. A one-shot session dies with its CLI, so run them in the foreground, or poll a background run until it finishes.

When something fails:
- Fix it inside steps 1-4's files only, and never weaken an assertion.
- A failure that also reproduces on a clean HEAD snapshot is pre-existing: report it with that evidence.
- In the summary, name every skipped or not-applicable case. path-long is Windows-only.

Adversarial self-review of this task's diff only. Load the adversarial-self-review skill, then check:
1. Rail 4. With no workspace, a worker's pre-flight differs only by one rev-parse of refs/heads/moe/task/<id>. Architect, QA and governor seats never reach provision_worktree or Initialize-MoeWorktree.
2. Fail closed.
- No refusal path reaches the taskless-launch decision or a CLI launch, and each calls report_blocked exactly once.
- worktree_stop never runs inside $(...), a pipeline or a subshell.
- The ps1 catch can never swallow the exit.
3. Data safety.
- Nothing deletes a directory this session did not add, a W whose branch has commits beyond the target, any branch, or W/.moe.
- Reuse never runs read-tree on a non-empty index.
4. Rail 3.
- No .moe path exists in W after create, re-add or a half-made finish.
- The control checkout's HEAD, index and files are untouched, and `git -C <control> config core.sparseCheckout` stays unset: the sparse config lives in W's worktree config only.
5. Concurrency: what happens if two wrappers provision the same task at once? Git's worktree add and its lock answer it, and the loser gets CREATE_FAILED. Confirm the loser can never remove the winner's W, because the removal runs only after this session's own add.
6. Cross-OS.
- D:\ vs /mnt/d spellings, with repair only on a raw mismatch.
- The msys-only path budget.
- PS 5.1 parsing and the BOM.
- set -e safety of every new sh line.
- The test fixtures' paths with spaces.
7. Parity. The seven codes, the detail sentences and the [worktree] line are identical in both twins. The DoD 5 diff is empty, and comments count toward it.
8. Size. Report `git diff --numstat` per file and net lines against the 400-net review cap; about 240 is expected.
If this review changes any byte, re-run step 5's command and submit that output to complete_task.

comments.author: worker-0062feec

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A worker seat reads `workspace` from the fresh claim's top level (WT-01), else from get_context's top level (WT-02); absent means shared mode. In worktree mode it provisions W = <git top>/.worktrees/<taskId> on moe/task/<taskId>. It creates W from the LOCAL refs/heads/<target> with --lock --reason 'moe <taskId>' --no-checkout --no-track -b, re-adds it on an existing branch without -b, or reuses a registered W as is (repair on a cross-OS spelling, and an empty-index W is finished). It then runs sparse '/*' '!/.moe/' and read-tree -mu HEAD, prints `[worktree] <created|reused|re-added> <W> on moe/task/<taskId>`, and launches the CLI as today. Before any W work it refuses, in this order: git < 2.38 (MOE_WORKTREE_UNSUPPORTED_GIT), project not the git top level (MOE_WORKTREE_PROJECT_NOT_TOP), control HEAD not refs/heads/moe/control (MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING), blank or missing target (MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED), task commits on another ref that the target lacks (MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH), the Windows path budget (MOE_WORKTREE_PATH_TOO_LONG). Any git failure is MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, and W/.moe present is MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT. Every refusal prints `[ERROR] <CODE>: <detail>`, calls report_blocked once, launches no CLI and exits 1. In shared mode a worker refuses with MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH only when refs/heads/moe/task/<taskId> exists and is not fully landed in HEAD; otherwise nothing changes.
acceptanceCriteria: WT-04T's suite scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs (task-dd5daa4b789645d29b192176390884be) passes unchanged under sh and ps1, run from both postflight harnesses.
Every pre-existing postflight case passes with its bytes unchanged.
The sorted MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ token sets of moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 are identical (empty diff).
invariants: Shared mode is unchanged except for the one MODE_MISMATCH guard on an unlanded task branch (epic rail 4).
No .moe path ever materializes in W, and provisioning never changes the control checkout's HEAD, index or files (rail 3).
The wrapper never deletes a directory it did not add in this session, never deletes a branch, and never removes a W whose branch has commits beyond the target.
Only worker seats provision; architect, QA and governor seats ignore workspace.

Correctness traps:
- DoD 5's grep reads comments too.
- The seat's own MOE_* env leaks into the wrappers under test unless scrubbed (step 5 does it).
- If ps1's git invocation doesn't resolve the suite's git stub, the git-old case fails. Report that against WT-04T; never edit the suite.

Timing: the two full harness runs take tens of minutes. Run them in the foreground or poll a background run until it finishes.
